## player\_transitioned

![Note.png](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/w/images/thumb/c/cc/Note.png/10px-Note.png)**Note:**

- Fires when a player has transitioned to a new chapter from the previous chapter in a campaign.
- While in coop or realism and the map is not a first session (`!Director.IsSessionStartMap()`), fires after a map reset because of mission loss.
- Fires alongside `player_spawn`, if the survivor has died from the previous chapter, this event fires first, and vice versa.

## non\_melee\_fired

`Called: Fires when a survivor attacks with a non-melee weapon.`

![Note.png](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/w/images/thumb/c/cc/Note.png/10px-Note.png)**Note:**

- Only fires once for each survivor; subsequent non-melee weapons being fired do not fire this event. Most likely used to detect if a survivor has used a non-melee weapon or not for non-melee achievements.
- It continues firing again after a map transition, reset and team swap.

- **userid**(short) \- User that fired a non-melee weapon

## infected\_decapitated

- **userid**(short) \- userid of the player who did the decapitation
- **weapon**(string) \- melee weapon name

- **upgradeid**(short) -
- **userid**(short) -

## vomit\_bomb\_tank

`Called: Fires when a survivor biled a tank using a vomit jar.`

- **userid**(short) \- userid of the player who biled the tank

## triggered\_car\_alarm

`Called: Fires when a survivor triggers a car alarm.`

- **userid**(short) \- user ID of player who activated car alarm

## panic\_event\_finished

## charger\_charge\_start

`Called: Fires when a charger starts charging.`

`Issues: Called more than once per ability use. For consistency, check ability_use`

`Issues: Can be called after charger_charge_end. Use ability_use for an alternative start-to-end relationship.`

## charger\_charge\_end

`Called: Fires when a charger stops charging.`

- **userid**(short) \- user ID of the charger

## charger\_carry\_start

`Called: Fires when a charger starts carrying a survivor while charging.`

![Icon-Bug.png](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/w/images/thumb/f/fc/Icon-bug.png/10px-Icon-bug.png)**Bug\*:** Does not fire when a charger stops charging right after it carries a survivor, usually happens when the survivor is near a wall. Subsequently, `charger_carry_end` does not fire.

- **victim**(short) \- user ID of the player who was charged

![Note.png](https://developer.valvesoftware.com/w/images/thumb/c/cc/Note.png/10px-Note.png)**Note:**

- Killing the charger or survivor being pummeled to death returns `rescuer` as 0.
- It only returns `rescuer` as the survivor's userid when the charger is staggered by a pipe bomb, explosive ammo, propane/oxygen tank.

- Using Stagger() on the charger returns `rescuer` argument as the charger's userid.

- **userid** (short) - user ID of the charger
- **victim** (short) - user ID of the player who was charged

[Left 4 Dead 2](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/boards/960510-left-4-dead-2) 3. Length of single player | | | --- | | **vanzip**16 years ago#1
Has anyone played the SP-version that can tell me the entire length of play? I don't have enough opportunities and the time to commit to on-line play. Played the SP demo and loved it, but spending $50 on four to five hours of gaming is not worth it to me at this time. Will wait for price drop if that's the case. | | **iammaxhailme**16 years ago#2
There REALLY isn't a point to single player if you have online. It's not a side-thing for online, it's the same thing, but with people.
Anyway, due to the way the game works, there is a lot of replay value, each campaign is different each time.
Best weapon combo in tf2: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7oUWPbS4450&feature=channel\_video\_title
http://www.last.fm/user/iammax | | **Spen**16 years ago#3
You won't get much out of the game without online play. Two of the game modes, Versus (Two teams taking turns playing Survivors through a Campaign while the other play as the Infected to stop them) and Scavenger (Two teams take turns trying to collect gas cans in a stuggle against time and the other team playing as the infected to slow them down) will not be available to you. I'm not sure about you, but I know I would get bored of Single Player fairly quickly, It's not exactly the main focus of the game. | | **Doober2**16 years ago#4
the SP is just the online campaign mode, with bots instead of people (and pretty poor bots at that).
But I'd say it's probably around 5 hours or so....I'd done 3 of the 5 campaigns and each one took around an hour
**Currently Playing:** Final Fantasy XIV | | **SavingParis**16 years ago#5
Eh...about an hour or so per campaign. It really depends on how much you want to replay it. If you played the first one, it's not going to be much different this time around, cept maybe a tad more re-playability. | | **Apocalypse89**16 years ago#6
It's fun to play each campaign once or twice on SP to learn the basic gameplay and layout of each level, and to notice the story and details of each level, but really there's no point buying this game if you don't intend to play it online.
"very primitive logical tasks that could do 7 years old boy." - kikoiko **(gs)**, talking about HL2.
**Board 402** | | **JennTheBox**16 years ago#7
Normal mode? About 40 minutes each campaign. They are all seriously about 40 minutes exact. Past that point, not sure. All depends if you play with bots or actual people. | | **IceMage20**16 years ago#8
Don't get this game if you're not going to play online. You know how there are some games that have great single-player modes, and then a multiplayer mode that feels incomplete and tacked on? Yeah, in L4D 1/2, it's the single-player that feels tacked on. Playing with bots all the time is not fun at all, and I wouldn't have gotten either game if it weren't for Versus.
_Click **here** to take the idiot test. ~ Glaurungd_
_^uh i think your link doesnt work, u should learn HMTL ~MooMoo321_ | | **sfcalimari**16 years ago#9
Yeah the game is not worth it to play offline for $50. The game is only fun if you play online. It's ok to play the maps offline on easy or normal with bots to learn the levels, but the bots are really dumb and the game is just way more fun if you play with other people, especially with people you know who aren't either poor players or griefers.
Each map does take about 40 minutes to an hour depending on how many times you die and have to restart a level. It wouldn't take any more time to play through a level online compared to offline. The bots rarely rescue you if you get knocked down by the enemies so actually you're less likely to restart if you are playing with humans who know how to play the game and actually bother to rescue one another..
I will now sell five copies of the Three EP's by the Beta Band. | | **mycoplasma**16 years ago#10
It's alot longer than TF2's single player. | - Topic Archived - Page 1 of 2 - [Last](https://gamefaqs.gamespot.com/boards/960510-left-4-dead-2/52370186?page=1) ## More Topics from this Board 1. # [Comprehensive Guide for My L4D2 Settings (COMPETITIVE SETTINGS)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aNbTO8xbr2Y)

**Visibility**: Public
**Uploaded by**: [Chupaflaba](https://www.youtube.com/@Chupaflaba)
**Uploaded at**: 2023-12-15
**Published at**: 
**Length**: 06:06
**Views**: 9978
**Likes**: 297
**Category**: Gaming

## Description

```
This video's purpose is to demonstrate and explain my auto exec, in game settings, as well as crosshair. I will be comprehensively explaining each and every setting and detail in the video so you can get a grasp and level up your gameplay.

cl_forcepreload "1"                                     "Preloads things to reduce lag"
cl_updaterate "100"                                     "Lerp setting
cl_cmdrate "100"                                        "Lerp setting"
rate "100000"                                           "Lerp setting"
cl_resend "1.5"                                         "Time it takes to disconnect"
cl_interp "0.0"                                         "Lerp setting"
cl_lagcompensation "1"                                  "Improves hit registration"
cl_interp_ratio "-1"                                    "Lerp setting"

bind "W" "+mfwd"                                        "Null cancelling movement ; Smoother movement"
bind "A" "+mleft"
bind "S" "+mback"
bind "D" "+mright"

alias +mfwd "dsp_volume 0;-back;+forward;alias checkfwd +forward"                     "Special script for directional volume"
alias +mback "dsp_volume 0;-forward;+back;alias checkback +back"
alias +mleft "dsp_volume 0;-moveright;+moveleft;alias checkleft +moveleft"
alias +mright "dsp_volume 0;-moveleft;+moveright;alias checkright +moveright"
alias -mfwd "-forward;checkback;alias checkfwd none"
alias -mback "-back;checkfwd;alias checkback none"
alias -mleft "-moveleft;checkright;alias checkleft none"
alias -mright "-moveright;checkleft;alias checkright none"
alias checkfwd "none"
alias checkback "none"
alias checkleft "none"
alias checkright "none"
alias none ""

snd_mixahead "0.01"                         "Lerp for sound"
dsp_enhance_stereo "1"                      "Better sound quality"
dsp_slow_cpu "0                             "Better sound quality"

mat_grain_scale_override "0.0"              "Boosts fps around fire and smoke"
r_dynamic "0"                               "Removes eye detail"
r_eyemove  "0"
r_eyesize "0"
r_eyeshift_x "0"
r_eyeshift_y "0"
r_eyeshift_z "0
cl_detail_max_sway "0"                      "Removes prop sway detail"

mat_monitorgamma "1.6"                      "Improves brightness"
mat_monitorgamma_tv_enabled "1"

bind mwheelup +jump                       "Binds jump to scrollwheel ; Improves bunny hopping on 100 tick servers"
bind mwheeldown +jump

alias "+fastmelee" "slot2;+attack;"       "Fast melee or pistol bind"
alias "-fastmelee" "-attack; slot1;"
bind "alt" "+fastmelee"
```

> Personally I love checking peoples stats and the stats are a great way to add near "endless" replayability to an already great game. But man they are so busted at times. I am aware you can use scripts to make easy mod deal damage and make bots have more health but the gun stats are just stupid.

I'm not even talking about using scripts to enable FF on Easy; The vanilla game literally counts FF on easy as "dealing damage", even though you aren't dealing any damage.

If you shoot your teammate point-blank with a shotgun on Easy difficulty, they'll be perfectly fine, but the game will still track it to your stats as if you just incapped them.

You can also get some stats updated from watching demo recordings. For example, if you watch a demo of someone playing Survival, and they get a better time than you have, _their_ time gets added to _your_ stats at the end, even though you're just watching the playback of a round.

The stats have been busted for most of the time the game's been out though, I remember that they were already inaccurate all the way back in 2016.

3. Host\_timescale Command

# Left 4 Dead 2 Host\_timescale Command

* * *

This command changes the "timescale" of the game - i.e. what speed the game processes/runs at. Setting this command to 2 would make the game run two times as fast (as-if it were in fast forward), whereas setting this command to 0.5 would make the game run in slow motion (half as fast).

## Host\_timescale Syntax

* * *

The syntax for the host\_timescale command is as follows:

host\_timescale \[timescale\]sv\_cheatsDefault Value: 1

This command has the following arguments:

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Timescale** | The number to multiply game time by. 1 is default (everything runs at normal speed). 3 would be 3x as fast, 0.25 would be 25% as fast (one quarter). |

### Looking for other commands?

Search our database of 117 Left 4 Dead 2 commands...

[Onwards](https://commands.gg/l4d2)

## Host\_timescale Examples

* * *

Find below working examples of the host\_timescale command.

* * *

host\_timescale 2

This command would make the game run two times as fast (as if it were in fast forward).

host\_timescale 0.5

This command would make the game run half as fast (as if it were in slow motion).

The story takes place in [Savannah](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Savannah "Savannah"), Georgia, after the events in [The Sacrifice](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Sacrifice "The Sacrifice"). The four survivors climb up the roof to witness the last rescue helicopter leave the rooftop of [The Vannah](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Vannah "The Vannah"). They decide to go to a mall, where a second evacuation point is located. While on their way, they learn each others names: [Ellis](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Ellis "Ellis"), [Coach](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Coach "Coach"), [Rochelle](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Rochelle "Rochelle") and [Nick](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Nick "Nick"). After an encounter with [Whitaker](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Whitaker "Whitaker"), the survivors enter the mall to discover that it is overrun, with all [CEDA](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/CEDA "CEDA") agents at the center either dead or infected. The group enters the mall's atrium to discover Jimmy Gibbs Jr.'s stock car and, following Ellis's plan, fuel up the car to break out of the mall where they head to [New Orleans](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), rumored to be the last standing city in America. The four then arrive at the raised bridge in [Rayford](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Rayford "Rayford"), where they meet [Francis](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Francis "Francis"), [Louis](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Louis "Louis") and [Zoey](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Zoey "Zoey"). The late [Bill](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Bill "Bill") sacrificed his life to raise the bridge, and [Louis](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Louis "Louis") had been wounded by a Witch as the group explored Rayford. Because the new survivors need to cross the bridge, they must find another way across and refill the generator. After battling through a wedding, the streets, and a "historical sewer", they meet up with the original survivors again, who help cover the new survivors while they fend off the Infected in order to fill the generator and lower the bridge. They continue driving until they reach [Griffin County](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Griffin_County "Griffin County"), where they find the highway is completely blocked by abandoned vehicles, thus forcing them to proceed on foot through miles of abandoned cars where they find a distant search light. The lights are revealed to come from [Whispering Oaks Amusement Park](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Whispering_Oaks_Amusement_Park "Whispering Oaks Amusement Park"). As they fight their way through the Park and navigate to its stadium, Coach comes up with an idea to use the concert equipment in [The Peach Pit](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Peach_Pit "The Peach Pit"), abandoned by [Midnight Riders](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Midnight_Riders "Midnight Riders"), to attract the helicopter pilot's attention. The plan works, and the Survivors manage to evacuate in the helicopter as the masses of Infected swarm the stadium. [![The Survivors of Left 4 Dead 2](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/b/b7/The_Survivors_of_L4D2.JPG/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/300?cb=20100131222411)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/b/b7/The_Survivors_of_L4D2.JPG/revision/latest?cb=20100131222411) The Survivors of _Left 4 Dead 2_. (From left to right: Ellis, Coach, Rochelle, and Nick) After being rescued, the helicopter pilot becomes infected, prompting Nick to shoot him and cause the helicopter to crash. The Survivors exit the wrecked helicopter to find that they have landed in a bayou. They discover a small [village](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Plank_Country "Plank Country"), where the villagers decided to fend for themselves, but ultimately failed as they were overrun. Working their way through the swamp, the survivors come across a crashed plane, dead military paratroopers, and infected swamp villagers. The previous survivors had informed any passerby to head to the [Plantation House](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Plantation_House "Plantation House"). When the survivors head there, they find a radio, which they use to contact [Virgil](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Virgil "Virgil") for rescue. After fending off the horde, Virgil blasts the Plantation gate open to allow the survivors to escape on his boat before the horde could overwhelm them. On their way to New Orleans, Virgil's boat runs low on fuel and drops off the survivors at [Ducatel](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Ducatel "Ducatel"), Mississippi to find gas. The survivors forget the gun bag, and the [local gas station](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Ducatel_Gas_Bar "Ducatel Gas Bar") is out of gas which forces them to go to the next [gas station](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Ducatel_Diesel "Ducatel Diesel") two miles away. After passing through an [abandoned sugar mill](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Ducatel_Sugar_Company "Ducatel Sugar Company") infested with Witches, they find the gas station. After collecting their fuel, they begin to head back when stormy weather hits. Going all the way back to the Burger Tank, Coach comes up with the idea to use the Burger Tank's sign to signal Virgil. They succeed, and Virgil arrives to pick them up before the Survivors are overwhelmed by the Infected. Virgil drops the group off at [New Orleans](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/New_Orleans "New Orleans"), where Coach is immediately reinvigorated as they see fighter jets in the sky, revealing that the military has not abandoned the city yet; Nick however is skeptical about their presence. They decide that the [bridge](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Veterans_Memorial_Bridge "Veterans Memorial Bridge") in the distance is the best chance of survival, but discover the corpses of non-infected people on the way. The survivors suspect that the military took over CEDA's pitiful attempts to contain the situation as they find themselves in an area being bombed by the military, and quicken their pace to the bridge. They interrupt a transmission on the bridge between the two military personnel: Papa Gator and Rescue 7, who suspect that the Survivors are [Carriers](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Carriers "Carriers"). Rescue 7 is prepared to carry the Carriers, and Papa Gator informs the Survivors that they are lucky as the Military had just left the area, and that they must reach the other side of the bridge for rescue. The Survivors fight through the Infected amassed on the bridge and reach Rescue 7. As he carries the Survivors out, the fighter jets bomb the bridge to prevent the Infected from leaving the city and the pilot takes the Survivors out to a military cruise ship at sea. [\[3\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-3) ## The Cover and Rating\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D2&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] [![The latest cover hand (left), the previous one (center), and the oldest known one (right).](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/b/b2/L4dcovers123.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/200?cb=20090804225430)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/b/b2/L4dcovers123.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20090804225430) The latest cover hand (left), the previous one (center), and the oldest known one (right). The cover of _Left 4 Dead 2_ is almost identical to the original _[Left 4 Dead](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead "Left 4 Dead")_ cover. The hand was modeled once again by former Valve artist Andrea Wicklund. The idea was to create a hand missing another two fingers along with the famous original missing thumb, resulting in a hand only holding up two fingers, further signifying the number two. The background's color was also changed to a lighter shade of green. Around June 2009, the ESRB told Valve that the new cover is unacceptable and the idea was changed to tucking the two unwanted fingers behind the hand to attain the desired effect, yet still keep the missing thumb. - The ESRB was asked why they still allowed the new cover with only the missing thumb, yet not accepting the two unwanted fingers and the thumb. The ESRB declined to comment.[\[4\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-4) Around July 2009, Valve decided to change the cover once again, making the two tucked-away fingers slightly more visible. The hand drastically changed as the background did which is now yellow. In the United Kingdom, the cover was changed to show the hand facing the opposite direction, as the two-finger sign towards the viewer is considered an insult. This cover design change does not apply with the New Zealand and Australian versions of the game even though the direction of the two-finger sign applies in those countries as well. In addition, the German and Japanese version of the cover features all of the fingers intact as it did with the first game due to the same censorship reasons that applied to the first game's cover. Australia and Germany censored _Left 4 Dead 2_, removing some features generally to do with violence: - Blood and gore: Virtually no blood is found after killing the Infected and it's impossible to remove any body parts by using weapons on them. Despite this, achievements for dismemberment were still included and can be awarded in the Australian version. - Fire and Explosive Effects: The Infected can no longer be set on fire and no damage is visible when hit with [Explosive Ammo](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Explosive_Ammo "Explosive Ammo") or the [Pipe Bomb](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Pipe_Bomb "Pipe Bomb"). Infected that the game registers as having been set on fire act in the same way as they would if on fire except that no fire is visible. - Bodies: After dying, the Infected disappears, often before they even hit the ground. - Infected: The [Riot Infected](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Uncommon_Infected#Riot_Infected "Uncommon Infected") is removed from the game because it "encourages violence against official authority" (despite them being actually private security employees). In the Australian version, the Riot Infected was eventually put back in with minor alterations to remove any connection to the official authorities. The Survivors need to look out for each other. ## Reception\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D7&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] _Left 4 Dead 2_ was universally acclaimed by critics, with a Metacritic score of 89/100 on both PC[\[5\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-5) & Xbox 360[\[6\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-6) based on 55 critic reviews and 76 critic reviews respectively. ### Awards\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D8&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] _Left 4 Dead 2_ was featured as one of Game Informer's top 50 games of 2009. Game Informer had this to say: "Ever wonder how far you could make it through the zombie apocalypse with just a [chainsaw](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Chainsaw "Chainsaw") and a [grenade launcher](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Grenade_launcher "Grenade launcher")? _Left 4 Dead 2_ has your answer. Everything about Valve's sequel to last year's intense co-op FPS is amplified, with gratuitous gore, tons of melee weapons, intensified finales and even more zombies. If you still think that this sequel came too soon, then you haven't cracked a clown zombie in the face with a cricket bat while protecting a lawn gnome." The Drunk Tank Podcast by [RoosterTeeth](http://roosterteeth.com/home.php) named _Left 4 Dead 2_ the best game of 2009. ### [Boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boycott "wikipedia:Boycott")\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D9&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] Shortly after Valve's announcement of _Left 4 Dead 2_, many fans were shocked of the idea due to the short period of time after the first _Left 4 Dead_ and the fact that the long promised SDK (which is essential to making new levels for Left 4 Dead) was being held back because of this. Hours after the announcement, fans gathered together and formed a group called [L4D2 Boycott (NO-L4D2)](http://steamcommunity.com/groups/L4D2boycott); the group reached 10,000 members in one week and 35,000 members in three weeks. The group believed that _Left 4 Dead 2_ should not be a separate game in order to keep the community whole, claiming that releasing a sequel would split the community. Their suggestion was to make _Left 4 Dead 2_ either an expansion pack that is either free downloadable content or not full-priced, citing a lack of new content and also voicing their preference to keep the original Survivors and maps. Many fans were also disappointed that Valve had yet to deliver the free DLC that they had promised. Valve informed the fans that they have been tracking their comments ever since the first announcement on June 1, 2009 and their response was that _Left 4 Dead_ will continue to be supported with downloadable content. This announcement caused some fans to believe that Valve saw the fans of _Left 4 Dead_ as boycotting the sequel only to get more free updates and save money. Valve also said that they are discussing the matter and are considering importing the original maps into _Left 4 Dead 2_; nothing regarding the original Survivors was mentioned. The boycott was not especially effective because the pre-order sales of _Left 4 Dead 2_ were 4 times larger than the pre-order sales of _Left 4 Dead._\[ _[citation needed](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Template:Citation_needed "Template:Citation needed")_\] The boycott has since been officially disbanded as the founders themselves said that they have done what they set out to do and are now sympathetic with Valve's work on _Left 4 Dead 2_, but however still maintain that they themselves will not buy the game. Despite stating this, one should note the irony that on the leaders' profiles it is noted that they both own and play _Left 4 Dead 2_.[\[7\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-7)[\[8\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-8) As of 2011, Valve has ported all six original campaigns from _Left 4 Dead_ to _Left 4 Dead 2_, playable with the original survivors. [No Mercy](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/No_Mercy "No Mercy") and [The Sacrifice](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Sacrifice "The Sacrifice") were ported to the game on October 5, 2010, while the rest were ported with the addition of [Cold Stream](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Cold_Stream "Cold Stream") on March 22, 2011. The campaigns are virtually identical to their original versions besides the addition of melee weapons (which were absent from the original game) and updated character icons. ## Gallery\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D10&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] ### Trailers\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D11&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] _Main article: [Left 4 Dead 2 Trailer](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2_Trailer "Left 4 Dead 2 Trailer")__See also: [Videos and Trailers#Left 4 Dead 2](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Videos_and_Trailers#Left_4_Dead_2 "Videos and Trailers")_ [![The blood and Smoker tongue is missing in the TV commercial (Bottom) but is in the Zombie Survival Guide (Top)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/e/e2/Nobloodorsmokert.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/185?cb=20091112002953)](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/File:Nobloodorsmokert.png "Nobloodorsmokert.png (190 KB)") The blood and Smoker tongue is missing in the TV commercial (Bottom) but is in the Zombie Survival Guide (Top) [![Left 4 Dead 2 teaser trailer from E3 '09.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/8/8e/L4D2_Teaser/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/185?cb=20120406010351)](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/File:L4D2_Teaser "L4D2 Teaser (13 KB)") L4D2 Teaser _Left 4 Dead 2_ teaser trailer from E3 '09. edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D15&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] - New [Main Characters](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Survivors#Left_4_Dead_2_Survivors "The Survivors"). - More [Infected](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Infected "Infected") per level. - Revamped gore system. - New [Common Infected](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Common_Infected "Common Infected") textures and models. - New [Special Infected](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Infected#Special_Infected "The Infected") textures and models. - New Special Infected (The [Charger](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Charger "Charger"), the [Jockey](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Jockey "Jockey") and the [Spitter](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Spitter "Spitter")). - New [Uncommon Infected](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Uncommon_Infected "Uncommon Infected") enemies. - More [guns](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons#Left_4_Dead_2 "Weapons"). - New [weapons tier](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons#Other_Tier "Weapons"). - [Melee weapons](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Weapons#Melee_weapons "Weapons"). - [Gauntlet crescendos](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Crescendo_Event "Crescendo Event"). - New [Gameplay Modes](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Gameplay_Modes "Gameplay Modes"). - Upgraded Graphics. - [_Counter Strike: Source_ weapons](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/International_Weapons "International Weapons") (German users were originally the only players who had this due to censorship, however, as of the last stand update, these weapons are available for everyone.). ### Downloadable Content\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D16&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section 2)")**. ### Split screen\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D17&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] Split screen play is fully supported on the Xbox 360, allowing the players to play both online and offline with a friend by using one console. On PC, split screen is unsupported, but still possible. Using an Xbox 360 controller for PC and some console commands, one can play only offline with a friend. Due to changes in the console, split screen online for PC is not possible, unlike _Left 4 Dead_ where split screen PC can be done both online and offline. Doing this requires a higher-end processor. ## Notes\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D18&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] - Valve decided not to give the game an elaborate sequel name due to the simplicity of the game. However, the team considered calling it _Back 4 More_.[\[9\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-OXM99-9) - The game takes place in Autumn as seen in a banner in the beginning of the trailer as well as various pieces of graffiti which are dated for early October. - In the trailer, one can see what appears to be Marine Corps or Navy F/A-18 Hornets bombing the Infected. The Infected can also be seen breaking through fenced barriers, implying Valve's statement that New Orleans had been relatively safe from the Infection before the events of _Left 4 Dead 2_. - [Valve](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Valve "Valve") seems to have reused the baseball bat hitting sound from the sound used in _Team Fortress 2_ which was also used in _Half-Life 2._ However, they have applied new, more authentic wooden sounds for it. - Upon seeing the campaign poster for [The Parish](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/The_Parish "The Parish") with all four Survivors standing together, _Game Informer Magazine_ commented; "Now the Black Guy is also the Old Guy and the office professional is wearing a suit instead of a tie. Yep, they're really mixing it up this time around." This statement might be seen as contradictory, implying that there are two Louises who became both Coach and Nick, but is simply commenting on the similar lineup of the main characters in relation to the previous game. - As seen in some gameplay videos, the "Dying Animation" of the Hunter and Smoker changed. Instead of flying away when being shot in the head like in the first _Left 4 Dead,_ they just fall on the ground like any other Infected. The Charger and Jockey can still go flying when killed, depending on how they moved before death. - Although the UK's boxart was changed due to censorship issues, the manual and the game avatar keep the original 'hand logo'. - The clues for how all of the game's campaigns related are less subtle than the ones for the campaigns in the first game which provided little to no obvious signs of how the Survivors ended up in each campaign with the exception of [Crash Course](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Crash_Course "Crash Course"). - Every time that you started _Left 4 Dead 2 up_, the loading screen, menu background animation and music will change to match one of the 5 campaigns.[\[10\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-10) - _Left 4 Dead 2_ was nominated for "Game of the Year" in the 2009 Spike Video Game Awards. It also won the best Xbox 360 Game. - _Left 4 Dead 2_ came third in _Screwattack's Top 10 Zombie Games_, beaten only by _Resident Evil 2_ and _Dead Rising_. - Though numerous areas of the game's campaigns appear in the opening scene, their appearance and order that they are shown is different. The differences included the Plantation's mounted gun being on the lower deck rather than the balcony above, the hotel having a room that has a health pack and several guns and the atrium in Dead Center's mall having many more floors than in the actual game. - Chet Faliszek once jokingly said that if the Infected in _Left 4 Dead 2_ were supernatural and undead, the game would be named _Left 4 Dead 2: The South Shall Rise Again_.[\[9\]](https://left4dead.fandom.com/wiki/Left_4_Dead_2#cite_note-OXM99-9) ## External Links\[ [Sign in to edit](https://auth.fandom.com/signin?redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fleft4dead.fandom.com%2Fwiki%2FLeft_4_Dead_2%3Fveaction%3Dedit%26section%3D19&uselang=en&metadata=article-registration-edit-article-section "Sign in to edit")\] [![An autographed copy of Left 4 Dead 2 given away during the "Dude Where's my Thumb 2" contest.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/f/fd/Signed_L4D2.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/150?cb=20100425190521)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/left4dead/images/f/fd/Signed_L4D2.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20100425190521) An autographed copy of _Left 4 Dead 2_ given away during the "Dude Where's my Thumb 2" contest. - The yearly achievement activity graph
shows how the total achievements earned by players in a game are spread out over time,
divided into years. It is displayed as a relative percentage of all achievements earned.


## Monthly achievement activity

[Purchase a premium subscription to get access to this graph and more.](https://playtracker.net/pricing/)

The monthly achievement activity graph
shows how the total achievements earned by players in a game are spread out over time,
divided into months. It is displayed as a relative percentage of all achievements
earned.

![](https://playtracker.net/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto/https://playtracker-apollo.fra1.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets%2Fplaytracker_main_bg.jpg)

## New users over time

[Purchase a premium subscription to get access to this graph and more.](https://playtracker.net/pricing/)

The new users over time graph shows the rate at which a game reached its current playerbase using the time when a user earned their first achievement. It is a rough approximation of lifetime sales. It is displayed as a relative percentage of all owners.

![](https://playtracker.net/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto/https://playtracker-apollo.fra1.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets%2Fplaytracker_main_bg.jpg)

## User interaction

Active in Left 4 Dead 2

Perfected Left 4 Dead 2

The user interaction graph shows interactivity data with up to three values. The first is "Played" which shows how many players have played the game for at least a minute. The second is "Active" which shows how many players have last played the game recently (2 weeks). The last is "Perfected" and shows how many players have completed all the achievements for this game, provided the game has achievement support (otherwise this value will not show). All three values are X% out of 100% where 100% are the total owners of the game.

The concurrent players graph shows how many players were playing a game at a given time, sampled from Steam. If only a date is given, it was a point in time on that date, not a peak or a sum of players. No internal PlayTracker data is used.


## Playtime distribution

[Purchase a premium subscription to get access to this graph and more.](https://playtracker.net/pricing/)

The playtime distribution graph showcases the distribution of users according to their total playtime, capping out at 100. It is displayed as a relative percentage of all owners that have that many hours of playtime. The maximum number of hours shown includes everything above itself.

![](https://playtracker.net/cdn-cgi/image/format=auto/https://playtracker-apollo.fra1.cdn.digitaloceanspaces.com/assets%2Fplaytracker_main_bg.jpg)

The popularity over time graph shows PlayTracker's own "Popularity" metric for a game over time. "Popularity" is calculated from values like total owners, active owners, concurrent players, and more. An active owner is valued much higher than an inactive owner in "Popularity" calculation. It scales linearly - there are no diminishing returns.


## Geography

[Purchase a premium subscription to get access to this graph and more.](https://playtracker.net/pricing/)

The Geography chart shows how popular a game is in countries where there is enough data available while adjusting for the number of users from that country. So, for example, if players from a country equal 2% of our total userbase, but players from that country that play this game are 3% of that game's userbase, the relative popularity score for that country will be 1.5. Also states absolute percentage of players from that country for that game.
